findings.title: Coerced return turns success into lasting closure
findings.claim: The warning presents forced return into the persecutors' communal creed as a re-entry that fixes the loss of flourishing: the final أَبَدًا gives the denied success an endpoint-free duration rather than describing a temporary relocation.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier أَبَدًا meets the same-surah permanence contrast at 18:35, while the return verb and milla noun meet the direct forced-return parallels at 14:13 and 7:88; the focus's فَلَاح carrier then names the blocked result as success, salvation, or attainment.
findings.reader_payoff: Threat, re-entry, and failed flourishing become one causal sequence: disclosure exposes the youths to coercion, return captures their communal direction, and the loss is described as enduring.
findings.containment: The literal alternatives of stoning and forced return remain intact. The finding does not make every use of return, milla, or permanence coercive, and it does not transfer the speaker's claim in 18:35 into the focus.

epistemic.reason: The core branch is supplied by a trusted anchored publication and exact focus surface evidence; the supporting reader walk and connection targets add relevant context but carry legacy or target-morphology qualifications.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Sonu belirlenmeyen, çok uzun veya kesintisiz bir zaman süresini bildirir.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus adverb أَبَدًا carries endpoint-free duration inside the final negation.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The supplied 18:35 connection places the same permanence field in a claim that a garden will not perish.
branch_activations.activation: The contrast makes the focus's unbounded duration attach to the threatened loss of success, so permanence describes the consequence of coercive return.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Forced return would make the loss of flourishing endure rather than remain a reversible change of location.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus does not endorse the garden owner's claim in 18:35, and this activation concerns duration, not every neighboring root branch.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Ayrılınan bir şeye geri gelme ve başlangıçtan sonra aynı işe yeniden yönelme çekirdektir.

branch_activations.independent_trigger: The supplied 14:13 and 7:88 parallels explicitly pair forced return with entry into a community's milla.
branch_activations.activation: The wider coercive-return pattern turns the focus verb from neutral movement into the threatened restoration of an imposed allegiance.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Return is experienced as being made to re-enter the order one had left under pressure.
branch_activations.boundary: This applies to the hostile religious-return construction, not to every occurrence of the return root.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Kişinin benimsediği inançlar ve bunlara bağlı yaşam kuralları düzenli bir bütün oluşturur.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus milla noun names the domain into which the youths would be returned.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The same supplied parallels make milla the destination of a coerced communal return.
branch_activations.activation: The destination is therefore a structured creed and way of life, not merely a physical place or social neighborhood.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The threat reaches the youths' adopted order of belief and practice, making the feared return a reorientation of life.
branch_activations.boundary: The finding does not claim that every communal designation or every use of milla has this coercive force.

findings.title: Enduring success as a contrary permanence

findings.mechanism: The focus occurrence of أَبَدًا carries the duration branch, while the retrospective 18:108 note supplies an independent wider counterpart in which enduring success is the condition from which no transfer is desired.
findings.reader_payoff: The final 'never' gains a visible counter-shape: it is not only emphasis, but the duration of a lost good when the direction of allegiance is reversed.
findings.containment: The supplied counterpart is a contextual contrast, not a claim that this ayah promises the same positive outcome or that the retrospective note independently verifies 18:108's full Arabic analysis.

epistemic.reason: The wider counterpart is present only as a prose retrospective support record; its Arabic and word-level alignment are not embedded in the packet.

findings.title: Exposure turns into domination
findings.claim: The focus verb يَظْهَرُوا۟ عَلَيْكُمْ lets emergence and overpowering meet: the wider 9:8 parallel shows that being revealed to the hostile group is the point at which it gains power over the addressed believers.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier يَظْهَرُوا۟ in the over/upon construction meets the exact 9:8 occurrence and its supplied hostile-dominance relation, changing the conditional discovery from visibility alone into exposure with immediate power consequences.
findings.reader_payoff: The opening condition becomes a threshold: once the hidden group is exposed, the threat is already moving toward control rather than merely being observed.
findings.containment: The focus still states a conditional threat and does not make every appearance verb mean domination; the target morphology of 9:8 is not independently supplied, so the cross-ayah relation remains qualified.

epistemic.reason: The exact target Arabic and authored relation are supplied, while the supporting HFT nomination is legacy-unbound and the target's morphology is explicitly unavailable.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Güç ilişkilerinde karşı tarafı yenerek onun üzerinde üstünlük ve denetim kurmayı anlatır.

branch_activations.independent_trigger: The supplied 9:8 target repeats the hostile over/upon situation and is described as direct dominance that removes restraint.
branch_activations.activation: The wider dominance scene gives the focus's exposure condition a power-bearing edge: discovery is the contact through which control becomes possible.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: If the persecutors appear over the youths, their visibility has already become a form of subjection.
branch_activations.boundary: This activates the power facet in the supplied construction; it does not erase the ordinary possibility of simple appearance or claim that all disclosure entails domination.

findings.title: The coercive threat has a speech-side form
findings.claim: The focus's bodily stoning threat can be read alongside the wider 60:2 picture, where hostile captors reach believers with both hands and tongues and wish their disbelief; coercion therefore presses through physical harm and abusive speech together.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier يَرْجُمُوكُمْ supplies the bodily projectile threat, while the exact 60:2 connection supplies hostile hands and tongues as an independent verbal-pressure trigger; the contact activates the speech branch without replacing the literal stoning.
findings.reader_payoff: The threat becomes a fuller pressure scene: harm can strike the body, while hostile speech works on allegiance and tries to make the addressed group resemble its attackers.
findings.containment: The focus verb remains a bodily stoning threat here. This is a qualified contextual resonance through 60:2, not a claim that يَرْجُمُوكُمْ lexically means verbal abuse in this ayah.

epistemic.reason: The target Arabic and authored connection are supplied, while the branch-specific reader-walk support is legacy-unbound and the relation is analogical rather than a local lexical substitution.
